verdicts.rationale: The abstract and introduction identify all listed anatomical, data, and MR imaging challenges.
The task description specifies all eight structures, pulmonary-vein inclusion, single-phase input, one click per structure, and the stated exclusions.
The architecture predicts segmentation and stopping jointly, recurs through the segmentation output, and permits overriding stopping.
The loss derivation explicitly decouples time steps and removes backpropagation through time; training pairs are generated from complete annotations on the fly.
The training-data and augmentation descriptions specify these growth targets and input corruptions while preserving output targets.
The data section confirms the sample counts, eight labels, acquisition institution, scanner model, and field strength.
The reported ages, mean resolution, resized dimensions, and anatomical basis of severity categories match exactly.
The experimental setup reports both train/test splits, four-fold training validation, and ensemble test predictions.
Interaction was simulated, with the stated best-of-40 selection rules for binary and multiclass models.
All severe-subject 20–HVSMR Dice values and comparison p-values match Table 1.
All severe-subject 48–HVSMR+ Dice values and the Iter–U versus U–Net+S significance threshold match Table 1.
Good mild/moderate performance is supported, but the multiclass significance findings concern severe subjects. Omitting that population restriction overgeneralizes the results.
The inference-time report gives precisely these timings and GPU hardware.
Optional vessel zones were removed from both segmentations before Dice calculation, leaving required regions for comparison.
The failure analysis and limitations describe all listed failure modes and pathology-dependent difficulties.
The discussion reports these multiclass limitations, presents the stopping-point explanation tentatively, and notes inherited binary tuning.
The authors explicitly propose a future actual-user study to evaluate accuracy and their interaction-speed and intuitiveness hypothesis.
This accurately attributes the authors’ qualified novelty claim and preserves its modality, population, and labeling scope.
The contributions describe prescribed evolution, teacher-forcing sequence loss, automatic stopping, and optional candidate selection.
